title: Frontend: Debounce
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Debounce. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({wait,calls,end}). Model trailing debounce with nondecreasing [time,value] calls and inclusive end. A timer due at a call timestamp fires first. Return emitted [time,value] entries. wait > 0. This deterministic clock model tests scheduling, not a live clock.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep a timer handle and clear/restart it on every call.
alternativeApproaches: Add leading/trailing options and prove that a single leading call does not accidentally trigger an unwanted trailing duplicate.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: One call; burst; latest arguments.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
